newsitem.title: USA: PP&L Susquehanna, Pa. nuke in restart mode.
newsitem.headline: PP&L Susquehanna, Pa. nuke in restart mode.

text.p: The 1,090 megawatt Susquehanna nuclear power unit 1 was in a startup mode as of early Monday following a shutdown for repairs which began in February, the Nuclear Regulatory Commission (NRC) said.

The unit, located in Berwick, Pa., was in startup mode and operating at one percent of capacity as of early Monday, but was "holding power level...due to a turbine bypass valve pressure regulator problem," the NRC said in its daily plant status report.
Susquehanna 1 was taken off line Feb 25 in anticipation of a loss of vacuum in the unit's main condenser.
A restart of the unit was interrupted last week for additional work on a residual heat removal system.
The adjoining unit 2, with a capacity of 1,094 megawatts, was operating at 88 percent of capacity as of early Monday as it coasted down to a scheduled refueling outage set to begin March 15.
The two Susquehanna units are jointly owned by PP&L and Allegheny Electric Cooperative Inc.
